overview.headline: Ballistic flight on the Moon without air drag

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a thrown ball on the Moon feels no drag because there is no air.
keyPoints.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that horizontal speed stays constant during flight when nothing pushes sideways.
keyPoints.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight and the ball moves x = U0 * t across the ground.

keyPoints.point: Students learn how vertical speed falls with time while height follows a curved path under gravity.
keyPoints.quote: The vertical speed is V = V0 - g * t, and the height is y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the highest point of flight comes from the height equation at the top of the rise.
keyPoints.quote: Putting that time into the height equation gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

keyTerms.gloss: Resistance from air that slows a thrown ball
keyTerms.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyTerms.gloss: Moving in free flight under gravity alone after launch

keyTerms.gloss: Steady pull that slows rising motion and causes falling
keyTerms.quote: Vertically, gravity slows the ball at a steady rate g.

keyTerms.gloss: highest position reached when upward motion stops
